VI.description:
Measure the connector pane of EVERY VI in a list file, in one run, and write the results to a text file. The read-only bulk form of lvpane_probe.vi, and the only way to learn what a pattern's slot geometry is\3A the pattern cannot be set through VI Server, so a pattern can only be measured on a VI that already uses it.
Input is a text file with one absolute .vi path per line. Output is one record per VI, `pattern|path|Terminal Bounds[] as XML`, records separated by `@@@`. A VI that fails to load contributes a record with pattern 0 rather than stopping the sweep - the error wire is deliberately NOT chained between iterations.
Driven by RunVIAsTopLevel, which can only set STRING controls, so both paths are built on the diagram.
MEASURED\3A about 200 ms per VI over vi.lib, and 500 VIs of the examples tree took some 18 minutes - the cost is loading each VI, so a heavy tree is slower per VI rather than bigger. While it runs the AI gRPC service does not answer at all\3A other calls fail port discovery with DeadlineExceeded on the port that just worked. That is LabVIEW being busy, not the service being down, and the sweep itself finishes and writes its file regardless of the client-side timeout on the call that started it.
KEEP THE BATCHES SMALL - 250 VIs, and harvest after each. Opening a VI reference LOADS that VI and closing the reference does not unload it, so a sweep accumulates VIs for as long as LabVIEW lives. Measured\3A 40 VIs took 8 s, 254 took 90 s, 500 took 18 minutes, and a second 500 killed LabVIEW outright about 12 minutes in, with roughly 1100 VIs loaded and nothing written - a batch that dies takes its whole result with it, because the file is written once at the end.

Control.description: Absolute path of a text file holding one .vi path per line.
Absolute path of the text file the records are written to. An existing file is replaced.
